reasons: Cited grant clauses support the compliant classification: § 13.1 names Customer, its Affiliates and contractors acting on their behalf with no notice or consent gate; § 13.2 gives a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free paid-up licence including modification and contractor-support rights; § 13.3 limits revocation/suspension to material uncured payment or use breach after notice and cure, and permits transfer to an Affiliate or successor under a Section 24-permitted assignment.

This satisfies the preferred position on every material term (affiliate/contractor scope, irrevocability of paid-up licences, breach-only revocation for subscription licences, successor transferability), so no redline or negotiation comment is appropriate.
Consistent with the claimed status, no redline was rendered and no comment issued; deterministic checks (affiliates covered, no at-will revocation) both pass.

The rationale reasonably notes the § 14.2 'revocable, non-transferable' Deliverable licence as a residual tension while correctly routing that point to the IP/ownership rule to avoid double-flagging the same commercial term.
